definitions: Plural form of 'caucus', referring to a meeting of supporters or members of a political party or movement, or a similar group.
In the context of US politics, a system for selecting delegates to the presidential nominating conventions, often involving local meetings where voters discuss and vote for candidates.
examples: The Iowa Caucuses are the first major electoral event of the presidential primary season.
Many states hold caucuses instead of primary elections.
The Democratic Caucuses saw a high turnout this year.
